`inactive_cell` treated only `Sides{Closed, Connected}` as closed on the left, so on a `TripolarGrid` (`Sides{Closed, CenterFolded}` / `Sides{Closed, FaceFolded}`, and the distributed `*FoldConnected` versions) cells at `j < 1` were active and the southern wall was not peripheral.

This PR adds `LeftClosedTopology = Sides{Closed, <:Union{CommunicatingSide, CenterFolded, FaceFolded}}` and uses it in `inactive_node.jl`. It also adds a test that fails on main.

The PR's original advection change is no longer needed: since #6275, main already treats folded topologies as left-bounded in advection.

body:
Resolves https://github.com/NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl/pull/1097#issuecomment-6421304575.

> `regular_faces` and `regular_centers` read the reference, step and offset of `range(c₁, c₂, length = N + 1)`. Neither the return type of range nor these fields are public: `range` happens to return a `StepRangeLen` for `Float16`, `Float32` and `Float64`, and a `LinRange`, which has none of these fields, for other number types such as `BigFloat` and `BFloat16`, so building any regular grid of those types failed with a `FieldError`.
> 
> `regular_nodes` now builds faces and centers with the public `StepRangeLen` constructor, from a reference and a step computed in `BigFloat` and rounded to `Float64`, or to the number type when it is wider. The reference is the node nearest zero, so that a node at zero is exact, and both stay independent of the halo, as the offset alone depends on it. With a `Float64` reference and step, the ends of `Float16`, `BFloat16` and `Float32` coordinates are exact. No public type is wider than `Float64`, so `Float64` nodes still take the extended-precision reference and step of range, now behind an explicit check that range returned a `StepRangeLen`, and are unchanged. `BigFloat` ends are exact to an ulp.
> 
> `Float32` nodes now round the coordinate between the `Float32` ends of the interval, rather than the decimal ends that range recovers from them, so some differ by an ulp from before.

body:
This PR removes all method ambiguities and makes the quality-assurance tests cover the whole package instead of hand-maintained module lists. It also includes the fix from #6373, generalised to `Field`s.

Supersedes #6373, which should be closed when this PR merges.

## Ambiguities (9 → 0)

- **`*` vs LinearAlgebra (6):** the location-free multiary operator now requires its first argument to be a 3D or 4D field. The ambiguities only arose for a 2D `AbstractField` (e.g. `ConstantField{T, 2}`) multiplied with matrices/vectors.
- **`copyto!` vs `SparseArrays.CHOLMOD.Dense` (2):** added disambiguating methods. `SparseArrays` is already a dependency.
- **`getbc` for fields reduced in x and z (1):** a condition located at `(Nothing, LY, Nothing)` gets `(j, k)` on west/east boundaries but `(i, j)` on bottom/top ones, so `getbc` cannot tell which argument is the `y` index.

## Boundary conditions reduced in x and z (supersedes #6373)

#6373 fixed this for `FieldTimeSeries` with an `XZReducedBoundarySeries{D}` wrapper. Here the wrapper is generic, `BoundaryConditions.XZReducedCondition{D}`, and covers both `Field`s and `FieldTimeSeries`:

- Regularizing a boundary condition wraps an x-z reduced `Field` or `FieldTimeSeries` used on dimension `D = 1` or `D = 3`, so `getbc` reads the first boundary index on west/east and the second on bottom/top.
- Each wrapped type extends `xz_reduced_getbc(condition, j, grid, args...)`.
- The wrapper adapts to the GPU, moves between architectures, splits across regions on multi-region grids, and is still found by `extract_field_time_series`. Boundary conditions display exactly as before.
- Used directly with `getbc` without regularization, an x-z reduced `Field` follows the existing `FieldTimeSeries` behaviour, which picks the slot from `Nz`. Before, it was a method ambiguity.

## Explicit imports

Replaced bare `using X` statements (181 implicitly imported names) in `Oceananigans`, `DistributedComputations`, `Models`, `NonhydrostaticModels`, `ShallowWaterModels`, `LagrangianParticleTracking` and `VarianceDissipationComputations`. The unused `using .VarianceDissipationComputations` in `Models` is dropped.

## Tests

- `test/unit/quality_assurance.jl` now runs `detect_ambiguities` and `check_no_implicit_imports` once on `Oceananigans` (both already recurse into every submodule), replacing the per-module lists and their commented-out entries.
- `test/time_stepping/boundary_conditions.jl` gets #6373's `FieldTimeSeries` test and a matching one for `Field`s. Each sets an x-z reduced condition on the east and top boundaries for `Nz = 1` and `Nz = 5`, then checks the halos.

On CPU, `time_stepping/boundary_conditions` and `unit/quality_assurance` pass (614/614). A smoke script also ran `NonhydrostaticModel` (with particles, Stokes drift, Coriolis, buoyancy and `VarianceDissipation`), `ShallowWaterModel` and `HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel`. Distributed code is only checked by loading the package; it was not run under MPI. Nothing was run on GPU.
